A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Narrow Gate study, with matching authors, core experiments, and substantial shared content. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original representation analyses, attention-knockout experiments, and activation-patching results across several vision-language models, including supplementary results.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical analyses and adds VILA-U comparisons, caption-embedding analyses, and masked-fine-tuning experiments.

M1.justification: V3 introduces [EOI]-masked fine-tuning of Chameleon-7B and Emu3 to reduce dependence on the narrow gate (Section 4.2). This is a new training intervention, distinct from the Emu3 preparation fine-tuning and activation patching already present in v2.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet, Flickr30k, MS-COCO, VQAv2, and LLaVA-instruct training data. The new semantic probes and fine-tuning experiments reuse existing data and task coverage; they do not introduce a new domain or input scenario.

E2.justification: VILA-U-7B changes from a cited model to an evaluated comparator in geometry, attention, and knockout experiments. Figure 6 adds ordinary fine-tuning as a comparison for masked fine-tuning. Conversely, the Janus/Pixtral activation-patching comparisons in v2 Figure SM4 disappear, although those models remain in other experiments.

E3.justification: V3 adds a masked-versus-standard fine-tuning study using 15,000 training examples and checkpoint-wise evaluation on 2,000 examples per task. It also introduces caption-embedding neighborhoods as a semantic reference. These are new experimental protocols; the principal retained benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New caption-embedding probes test whether semantic localization extends beyond class labels, while masked fine-tuning tests whether dependence on [EOI] can be reduced. V2's progressive layer-window knockout analysis and supplementary Janus/Pixtral patching analysis are removed (Figures SM3 and SM4).

E5.justification: Both versions retain median/interquartile-range reporting for cosine similarity and the same statistical clustering procedure. Neither introduces benchmark seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or uncertainty estimation for the training curves.

E6.justification: Retained Table 1 rows have unchanged scores. V3 adds caption-alignment and fine-tuning recovery curves, plus VILA-U results: its MS-COCO score is 0.61 without ablation, 0.61 with [EOI] ablation, and 0.02 with all-image attention ablation (Table A3). Results from v2 Figures SM3 and SM4 are removed.

T1.justification: Equation (2) generalizes neighborhood overlap from same-class neighbor agreement to overlap with neighborhoods in a reference representation, enabling caption-embedding comparisons. The ImageNet specialization remains equivalent. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: V3 makes native versus non-native multimodal training central to the main claims, refining v2's broader multimodal-output versus text-output framing. It also adds the contribution that targeted fine-tuning can reduce narrow-gate dependence, extending the paper beyond identifying and steering the bottleneck.

C2.justification: V3 develops a three-factor explanation involving output objectives, training history, and visual tokenization, with stronger claims about architectural origins. It adds explicit limitations concerning communication direction and untested architectures, and develops masked fine-tuning as mitigation beyond v2's speculative CLIP-based safeguard.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds caption/VQA prompts, VILA-U specifications, masked-fine-tuning hyperparameters, and previously unspecified Emu3 LoRA rank and alpha. The code-release statement changes from future release to availability. Conversely, the full ImageNet class list and detailed metric/preprocessing appendix are removed; these omissions do not establish changed experimental settings.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion is largely retained. V3 adds references concerning model backbones, multimodal interpretability, representation geometry, and text embeddings, while dropping the transformer-circuits and controlled-generation references. VILA-U was already cited in v2, but receives a more substantive comparative role.

P1.justification: V3 extensively rewrites the abstract, methods, results, and discussion around native/non-native terminology. Related work moves to Appendix A, semantic probing becomes a separate subsection, and model editing and robustness receive a dedicated section. The appendices are also reorganized.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, with widespread figure and table resizing and relocation. Emu3 panels move into main Figures 3 and 4; new training and caption-alignment displays appear, Figure A3 gains a comparison column, and old Figures SM3 and SM4 disappear.

improvement.justification: The native/non-native framing better accommodates the comparator evidence, and the caption probes and controlled fine-tuning experiment strengthen the paper's account of localization and its modifiability. These gains are moderated by removed diagnostic and reproducibility details. V3 also drops v2's explicit Emu3 VQAv2 exception despite unchanged scores: [EOI] ablation yields 0.48, versus 0.42 for all-image attention ablation, contradicting its generalized interpretation in Section 3.4.
